_about: Public-domain Martin Chemnitz (1522-1586), Lutheran theologian of Brunswick, for the Word Hoard: two Elizabethan English translations, A Discouerie and Batterie of the Great Fort of Unwritten Traditions (from his Examen of the Council of Trent, translated by R. V., 1582) and A Substantial and Godly Exposition of the Lords Praier (Cambridge: John Legate, 1598), from Internet Archive scans of Early English Books. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 39 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

chemnitz-discouerie-batterie-1582: A Discouerie and Batterie of the Great Fort of Unwritten Traditions: otherwise, An Examination of the Counsell of Trent touching the Decree of Traditions, done by Martinus Chemnitius in Latine and translated into English by R. V. (London: Thomas Purfoot and William Pounsonbie, 1582)
chemnitz-lords-praier-1598: A Substantial and Godly Exposition of the Praier commonly called the Lords Praier, written in Latin by D. Martine Chemnitius, newly translated out of Latine into English (Cambridge: John Legate; catalogued 1598)

_excluded.chemnitz-other: His Latin works (De Duabus Naturis 1580, the Examen ed. Preuss 1861); Christian and Bogislav Philipp von Chemnitz; the 1971-89 Concordia translations (in copyright); a mislabelled 'Concordia' item dated 1537
